answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks enforce topological cut verifications alongside game-theoretic multi-agent auditing. Agents stake capital upon a validator mesa, reaching an operational zenith where peer clusters audit connectivity bottlenecks. When suspicious subgraphs fail graph-cut thresholds, automated stake slashing destroys fraudulent deposits. Because validating independent cuts requires superlinear attacker cost scaling with network density, malicious node proliferation yields bankruptcy rather than an illicit safe haven.
